sections.h2: Does Missouri charge an estate tax?
sections.html:
Missouri imposes no estate tax for any death since the start of 2005, and no state return has to be filed for those deaths. The revenue department explains that the state tax was tied to a federal credit, and the IRS stopped allowing that credit for deaths after 2004.

The mechanism sits in RSMo 145.011. It taxes the transfer of an estate with Missouri tax situs at the maximum state death tax credit under Internal Revenue Code Section 2011. The federal credit fell to 75 percent for deaths in 2002, 50 percent in 2003, 25 percent in 2004 and zero from 2005 on, which left the Missouri figure at zero. The department adds that if the IRS ever reinstates the credit, a Missouri return would be required again under sections 145.011 to 145.955.

sections.h2: Is there a federal estate tax that could reach a Missouri house?
sections.html:
Federal estate tax applies only to estates above the basic exclusion amount. The IRS lists $15,000,000 for 2026 deaths, following the law signed on July 4, 2025. Most family homes in Missouri fall far below that line. A married couple can also carry over an unused exclusion to the surviving spouse by electing portability on a timely filed return.

Federal basic exclusion amount by year of death, from the IRS estate and gift tax page
Year of deathBasic exclusion amount
2022$12,060,000
2023$12,920,000
2024$13,610,000
2025$13,990,000
2026$15,000,000

An estate over the threshold files Form 706. If the executor files one, the beneficiaries generally receive a Schedule A on Form 8971 showing the estate tax value of what they inherit, and they must use it as their starting basis.

sections.h2: How can heirs get an inherited Missouri house sold?
sections.html:
The route depends on the size of the estate and on whether anyone has been appointed to act for it. Two paths in the Missouri statutes cover most house sales by heirs.

Two Missouri routes to selling a decedent's real estate, based on the revisor's statutes
RouteWhat triggers itStatute
Small estate affidavitEstate, less liens and debts, of $40,000 or less, with 30 days passed since death and no application for letters pending or grantedRSMo 473.097
Petition to sellAn executor or administrator asks the probate court for authority to sell real property of the estateRSMo 473.493

Under the small estate route, distributees can prove their right to the land by filing a copy of the affidavit and the clerk's certificate with the recorder of deeds in each county where the land lies. The affiant must post a bond unless the court finds one unnecessary, pay the filing fee, and cover estate debts. When the property listed in the affidavit exceeds $15,000, the clerk publishes a notice to creditors once a week for two weeks.

sections.h2: What does a court-ordered sale look like?
sections.html:
When letters have issued, RSMo 473.493 lets the executor or administrator file a petition stating why the sale is needed and describing the property. The court sets a hearing, and notice goes by ordinary mail or publication to heirs and devisees whose names appear in the file and to anyone else the court directs.

  • If publication is ordered, it runs once a week for four consecutive weeks.
  • The hearing then falls no earlier than the thirtieth day and no later than the forty-second day after the first insertion.
  • At the hearing, on satisfactory proof, the court may order the sale of all or part of the property.
  • When a mortgage secures a claim that is due, the court may order a sale subject to the mortgage with the lender's consent, and that consent releases the estate from any later deficiency.

Your probate attorney will tell you whether a petition is needed or whether the will already gives the personal representative power to sell.

sections.h2: What tax do heirs pay after selling an inherited Missouri house?
sections.html:
The federal gain is the sale price minus basis, and basis for inherited property is generally the house's worth when the owner died, under IRS Publication 551. A house worth $200,000 at death and sold for $205,000 shows $5,000 of gain, regardless of what the original owner paid decades earlier. The IRS directs readers who inherited property to Publication 551 and to Topic 409 for holding period details.

On the state side, Missouri lets an individual subtract 100 percent of federally reported capital gains from federal adjusted gross income, per the Department of Revenue. That subtraction is available to individuals and not to trusts, so who holds title when the sale closes matters. If the sale happens inside the estate, ask the preparer how the estate's income is reported.

Missouri imposes a fiduciary income tax on income earned by an estate or trust. A resident estate that must file federal Form 1041 files a Missouri fiduciary return, and a nonresident estate must file when it has $600 or more of Missouri-source gross income.

sections.h2: What paperwork should heirs gather before listing?
sections.html:
• A certified death certificate and the date of death, which anchors the basis figure.
  • Letters testamentary or of administration, or the small estate affidavit with the clerk's certificate.
  • An appraisal or other documented fair market value as of the date of death.
  • The deed or legal description of the property for the recorder of deeds.
  • Any Schedule A from Form 8971, if the estate filed a federal return.
  • Payoff figures for any mortgage, tax or lien on the property.

A deed goes on file with the recorder of the county that holds the land under RSMo 442.380. RSMo 442.400 adds that an unrecorded instrument is valid only between the parties and anyone with actual notice, so the buyer's deed should be filed promptly. A probate attorney in the county where the decedent lived can confirm the filing order for your particular estate.

faqs.q: Is there a Missouri estate tax for deaths in 2026?
faqs.a: No. The revenue department reports that no Missouri estate tax applies to any death since 2005, and no return is required. A return would be required again only if the IRS reinstated the federal state death tax credit.

faqs.q: How large must an estate be before federal estate tax applies?
faqs.a: For 2026 deaths the IRS basic exclusion amount is $15,000,000. Estates under that amount owe no federal estate tax, though a spouse may still file to elect portability of an unused amount.

faqs.q: Can heirs sell a Missouri house without opening probate?
faqs.a: Sometimes. If the estate, less liens and debts, is $40,000 or less and 30 days have passed since death with no letters sought, distributees can use the small estate affidavit under RSMo 473.097 and record it with the recorder of deeds.

faqs.q: What is the tax basis of a house I inherited?
faqs.a: Generally what it was worth at the owner's death, or on the alternate valuation date if the estate chose one. Beneficiaries of an estate that filed Form 706 usually receive a Schedule A with the value.

faqs.q: Does Missouri tax the gain when an heir sells an inherited house?
faqs.a: Missouri lets eligible individuals subtract 100 percent of federally reported capital gains from federal adjusted gross income, using Form MO-A with Form MO-1040. Trusts cannot claim that subtraction.
